record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: In a setting with no localized bound-state solutions, such as a non-negative localized smooth potential perturbed by a defocusing nonlinear term where one expects global existence and no localized solutions beyond known small-data cases, can one construct the scattering matrix and use it to recover both the potential and the nonlinear term?

evidence.quote: Problem 2 Let us consider a simpler situation where there are no bound states solutions to the in the equation. For example, it is expected (still open) that if a non-negative localized smooth potential is perturbed by a defocusing nonlinear term, there will be global existence and no localized solutions in many cases. Certainly, this is known for small initial data. So, there should be no problem in constructing the Scattering Matrix and finding the Potential and the nonlinear term as well.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger-type Cauchy problem on $\mathbb{R}^d$,
$$ i\,\partial_t u(t,x) = -\Delta u(t,x) + V(x)\,u(t,x) + F\bigl(x,|u(t,x)|^2\bigr)\,u(t,x), \qquad u(0,x)=u_0(x),$$
where:
- $V:\mathbb{R}^d\to[0,\infty)$ is a non-negative, compactly supported (or sufficiently rapidly decaying) smooth potential;
- $F:\mathbb{R}^d\times[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is a smooth, compactly supported (in $x$) defocusing nonlinearity, i.e., $\partial_s F(x,s)\ge 0$ and $F(x,0)=0$, satisfying standard growth/regularity assumptions ensuring local well-posedness in a suitable Sobolev space.

Assume that in this regime there are no localized (bound-state) solutions: every finite-energy solution exists globally and scatters, so that for every $u_0$ in an appropriate space there exist asymptotic free states $u_\pm$ with
$$ \bigl\| u(t,\cdot) - e^{it\Delta} u_\pm \bigr\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)} \longrightarrow 0 \qquad \text{as } t\to\pm\infty.$$
The (nonlinear) scattering operator $S: u_-\mapsto u_+$ is then well-defined on a dense subset of the relevant function space.

Question. Construct the scattering operator $S$ rigorously in this defocusing, no-bound-state setting, and prove that knowledge of $S$ (on, e.g., a dense set of small or generic asymptotic data) uniquely determines both the linear potential $V(x)$ and the nonlinear term $F(x,s)$. In other words, show that the map $(V,F)\mapsto S$ is injective on this class, and provide a reconstruction procedure recovering $V$ and $F$ from $S$.
artifact.category_tag: Inverse scattering for nonlinear Schrödinger equations
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: for generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equations with compactly supported potentials depending on the wave function, unique recovery of the potential from scattering data has been established, and singularities/jumps of the nonlinearity can be recovered from the high-frequency behavior of the reflection coefficient. However, in the full generality stated (general defocusing perturbation of a non-negative smooth localized potential, with global existence and absence of bound states still conjectural beyond small data), the simultaneous reconstruction of both V and F appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Inverse scattering for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation II. Reconstruction of the potential and the nonlinearity in the multidimensional case
status_evidence.snippet: Reconstruction of the potential and the nonlinearity for nonlinear Schrödinger equations in the multidimensional case.
status_evidence.claim: Partial reconstruction results for both potential and nonlinearity in multidimensional NLS exist.

status_evidence.title: Inverse scattering transform for the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with local and nonlocal nonlinearities
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes inverse scattering transform via Riemann-Hilbert problem for defocusing NLS with local and nonlocal nonlinearities.
status_evidence.claim: Inverse scattering machinery for defocusing NLS continues to be actively developed (2025).
